subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in session PIN authentication gate, or should this remain a plugin-level policy pattern?
rationale: The request crosses core config, secret handling, transcript redaction, framework tool blocking, and session lifecycle semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core session auth design
options.body: Define and implement a core opt-in session auth primitive with a trusted verifier, SecretRef-compatible secret handling, reset semantics, docs, and tests.

options.title: Prototype as plugin policy first
options.body: Keep core unchanged for now and validate the use case through a code plugin using before_tool_call plus plugin session state, accepting that it is not a uniform core guarantee.

options.title: Decline PIN gate for now
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide the PIN model gives a misleading security signal or does not fit OpenClaw's auth threat model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core session auth design
recommendation.body: Define and implement a core opt-in session auth primitive with a trusted verifier, SecretRef-compatible secret handling, reset semantics, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest overlapping history across strict config validation, session reset behavior, and adjacent auth/session state, making him the best available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
